channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: [8] Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Takashi Taniguchi, Amir Yacoby

Authors: Seung Hwan Lee, Shaowen Chen, Andrew T. Pierce, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Studies spin order via magnons in graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterostructures, relevant to user's broader interests.

Tags: #magnons #graphene #quantum_hall #heterostructure #magnetic_order

Abstract: Magnons in quantum Hall ferromagnets can be used as a very sensitive probe of magnetic order. Thus far, this technique has only been applied to single material systems. Here, Lee et al extend this to a heterostructure, using magnons generated in a monolayer of graphene to detect spin order in bilayer graphene.
